result.headline: Throttle command dropped to 0 at 98.3 s and stayed there; ch2 followed it; pitch loop degraded from about 106 s.
result.explanation: The first lasting control change is the throttle command going 57% to 0% at 98.282 s with no mode event. Motor channel ch2 simply followed it. What commanded zero is not in the recording.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT propulsion.throttle was varying, then held 0 from t=98.282 s to the end of the recording (19.275 s, 50 samples)
evidence.shows: The throttle command went to zero and stayed there. No mode change or event is recorded near it.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT actuator.output[ch[2]] was varying, then held 1100 from t=98.705 s to the end of the recording (18.976 s, 58 samples)
evidence.shows: ch2 dropped to 1100 us about 0.42 s after the throttle, i.e. it followed the command.

evidence.quote: ROLE actuator.output[ch[2]] follows propulsion.throttle (correlation 0.998 over the recording): it serves that loop
evidence.shows: ch2 is the propulsion output. The 0.994 correlation at lag 0 through 97.9 s shows it tracked throttle normally before the drop.

evidence.quote: SHIFT actuator.output[ch[1]] changed level for good at t=107.525 s: median 1497.5 before, 1247 after us (17.3x its variation before)
evidence.shows: The pitch-loop output (ch1) shifted about 9 s after the throttle cut, together with a pitch setpoint shift and worse pitch tracking.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT vehicle.airspeed = 0 for the whole recording (1405 samples)
evidence.shows: The airspeed signal never worked. It is a standing deficiency and may be why the controller could not tell what the thrust loss did.

checked.check: compare at 98.282 s: what changed at throttle drop
checked.result: Throttle 57 -> 0 (frozen, z 19). ch2 1568 -> 1100 (spread 0). Roll setpoint also moved.

checked.about: Motor output channel ch2 as the fault

checked.result: Throttle was varying 43-62% until 97.461 s, then 0 at 98.282 s. ch2 stayed varying until 97.981 s, then held 1100 us at 98.705 s.
checked.about: Throttle command cut as the earliest sign

checked.check: sequence 104-109 s and compare at 107.525 s
checked.result: ch1 left its baseline at 106.08 s. Pitch tracking error went from 5.805 to 6.807 deg and yaw tracking got worse (ratio 2.77). Altitude median fell from 48.159 to 47.313 m.
checked.about: Pitch loop is a later effect of lost thrust

checked.result: The only events are the start-up warnings at 0.804 s. At 10 s the roll setpoint median stepped from 1.24 to 33.49 deg and the velocities changed together. This looks like a manoeuvre, and velocity returns to large values later.
checked.about: Early 10-15 s anomalies as a fault

effects.quote: CONSTANT actuator.output[ch[2]] was varying, then held 1100 from t=98.705 s to the end of the recording (18.976 s, 58 samples)
effects.why: ch2 follows the throttle command, so the hold at 1100 us is a consequence of the zero throttle.

effects.quote: SHIFT actuator.output[ch[1]] changed level for good at t=107.525 s: median 1497.5 before, 1247 after us (17.3x its variation before)
effects.why: The pitch loop reacts later, probably to loss of thrust and altitude. The recording does not show it as an independent fault.

effects.quote: SHIFT vehicle.altitude[relative] changed level for good at t=108.129 s: median 49.93 before, 44.368 after m (5.3x its variation before)
effects.why: The altitude drop follows thrust loss and is a consequence.

next_action.why: This recording shows what changed but not who commanded throttle to 0. The onboard mode, failsafe and battery data would separate a deliberate or failsafe cut from a fault.

data_requests.what: Autopilot onboard log with mode, failsafe, RC input and battery/ESC telemetry
data_requests.why_needed: Separates a commanded or failsafe throttle cut from a propulsion fault. The recording has only 2 start-up events and no later mode changes.

unobservable.fact: Physical state of the motor, ESC and wiring on ch2
unobservable.why_it_matters: The recording shows only the commanded PWM, so a physical propulsion fault cannot be excluded.
unobservable.how_to_observe: Inspect the motor, ESC and connectors, and read the ESC error log.

hypotheses.claim: Throttle command went to 0 at 98.3 s from the controller or operator side, with no recorded reason.
hypotheses.because: Earliest lasting change at 98.282 s. ch2 and pitch/altitude changes follow it.

hypotheses.claim: The ch2 output or motor/ESC failed on its own.
hypotheses.because: ch2 tracked throttle at 0.994 until the drop and then went to 1100 us, as a zero command would make it.
hypotheses.observed_at: actuator output command, not the physical ESC

hypotheses.claim: Low battery voltage triggered a throttle cut or limit.
hypotheses.because: A Low voltage warning appears at 0.804 s (start-up). No voltage signal is in the recording to test it.

hypotheses.claim: Airspeed never worked, so the controller flew without airspeed and the later loss of control was not caught.
hypotheses.because: Airspeed is constant 0 for the whole recording. This is a standing condition, not an onset.

hypotheses.claim: The pitch loop (ch1) failed independently around 107 s.
hypotheses.because: It shifted about 9 s after the throttle cut, along with altitude loss and worse yaw tracking.

events.what: Throttle command 57% to 0%, held to end
